title: Preprocessors: Canny in core, and looking at your map
hook: Canny's thresholds aren't fractions of white. Learn what they are measured in, how to preview a control image, and what a bad map does.

verified.claim: The lab's Canny gives the same edge map as kornia.filters.canny 0.9.0, pixel for pixel, on the lab's noisy scene at four threshold pairs.
verified.ref: kornia.filters.canny, compared in a side script

verified.claim: A straight step needs contrast above high_threshold / 2.59 to start an edge: 0.3 fails and 0.31 passes at high 0.8, 0.38 fails and 0.39 passes at high 0.99.
A low threshold above the high threshold raises an error in kornia, even though the node's sliders allow it.
The node's sliders run from 0.01 to 0.99, defaults 0.4 and 0.8.
The hint is fitted with common_upscale, crop center, and resized by nearest-exact by default.
The Canny ControlNet 1.1 was trained on Canny with random thresholds.
d_canny_preview ran on a CPU here and validates.

unchecked: We ran no ControlNet for this lesson. How a noisy or empty map changes a picture is described from what the map contains, and is not measured. The scene in the lab is synthetic.
Core's pose nodes were only found by name and not read. No core preprocessor for line art, soft edges or scribbles rests on a search of node names, not on reading every file.
The share of edge pixels that suits a given ControlNet is not something we measured. The 4% to 12% in the browser lab is that lab's exercise, not a rule.
